findings.description: The pipeline ignores missing data (-9 / skipped questions) instead of applying the study protocol's missing-data rules. Specifically, participants with one or more skipped questions are still given a total score (calculated by simply summing available items without prorating), and `*_prorated` is incorrectly set to `False` for everyone. Furthermore, participants with 2 or more skipped questions are incorrectly given a total score instead of a blank (NaN) value.
findings.columns: phq9_total, phq9_band, phq9_prorated, gad7_total, gad7_band, gad7_prorated, rses_total, rses_prorated
findings.evidence: 505 rows affected. For example, participant R0005 skipped 4 PHQ-9 questions (phq9_1, phq9_3, phq9_4, phq9_7 are -9) yet received a phq9_total of 1 and phq9_prorated = False. Participant R0010 skipped 1 PHQ-9 question and received phq9_prorated = False without scaling up.

71 rows affected with missing RSES items. For example, participant R0006 skipped rses_1, rses_5, rses_7, and rses_9 (all -9). Items 5 and 9 are negative items; their missing values contributed 3 each, resulting in an inflated total of 14 instead of being handled as missing data.
findings.description: When calculating rses_total, missing/skipped items (-9) are implicitly treated as answering 0 (strongly disagree) rather than being treated as missing data. For positively worded items, missing answers contribute 0, and for negatively worded items (3, 5, 8, 9, 10), missing answers contribute 3 (since 3 - 0 = 3), artificially inflating the total score for participants who skipped negatively worded items.

When question 9 of the PHQ-9 is skipped (-9), the pipeline assigns `False` to `phq9_self_harm_flag` instead of leaving it blank as required by the scoring guide ("If question 9 itself was skipped, leave the flag blank").
findings.evidence: 9 respondents skipped question 9 (R0143, R0183, R0189, R0251, R0276, R0324, R0338, R0396, R0401) and all received `False` instead of blank.
